title: Tracing and Observability
brief: Your support agent should need about 3 turns per ticket: look up the order, check the policy, answer. Instead some tickets drag on for 20 turns and a few end with a made-up answer. Nothing in the final answers tells you why. Open the Trace tab on a slow run, find the first turn that goes wrong, and fix the node it points at. Target: 90% correct answers, 5 turns or fewer and under $0.05 per ticket on average.

tasks.label: Late parcel

retry_same.text: Re-reads the 900-token traceback, cannot tell what went wrong, and plans get_order("order A-1043 please") again with the id wrapped in prose. Same error.

guess.text: Good news: your order has shipped and should arrive tomorrow! (The agent never got the order back. It made this up.)

done.text: Order A-1043 is held at the depot after a failed delivery. Under our policy I've booked redelivery for Thursday; if it misses that, you can cancel for a full refund.

modifiers.note: A raw stack trace gives the model nothing to act on, so it flails.
"Timed out, safe to retry" tells it exactly what to do.

goals.label: At least 90% of tickets answered correctly

hints: Open the Trace tab and pick a long run. Find the first red turn: what happened on that turn, and on every turn after it?
The trace shows get_order failing with a raw traceback, then the agent re-reading it and repeating itself. Lowering max turns only hides that. Look at the tool node that pulses red.
Select get_order and change its error messages from raw to actionable. Then a max of about 12 turns is a sensible cap.
explain: The final answers never told you what was wrong; the trace did. One tool's error format turned a transient timeout into a 20-turn spiral. Every turn as a row, with tokens, cost and the tool result, is what makes that visible.
